newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French-Belgian Dexia has money to grow.
newsitem.headline: French-Belgian Dexia has money to grow.

text.p: Dexia, a Belgian-French group specialised in credits to local authorities, plans to continue its foreign expansion for which it has 60 to 80 billion Belgian francs available.

"We have the ambition to continue our international expansion via takeovers or the acquisition of new activities," Francois Narmon, chief executive officer of the Belgian arm of the group told a news conference.
"We see a lot of growth possibilities on all European markets with the exception of our home markets France and Belgium, notably in Germany, Scandinavia and Spain," Narmon said.
He added the group had no need for a capital increase to finance its expansion and that it had 60 to 80 billion Belgian francs available for takeover operations.
"Our problem is not a lack of own funds but an excess of own funds. American investors have often pointed to the fact that we are over-capitalised," Narmon said.

He said he expected Dexia to remain a French-Belgian group which would take stakes in other banking groups but specified he expected no widening of the core shareholding alliance between Belgian publicly-owned bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) and French Credit Local de France (CLF)
"I do not expect an enlargement of the core shareholding structure. We will remain a French-Belgian group," Narmon said.
Earlier this year, Dexia made a first move abroad when it took a 40 percent stake in Italian Crediop, a unit of Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino.
Crediop is the second-largest lender in the Italian public services financing sector.
